label: Socket
description: A WebSocket endpoint: each connection opened at its path starts one run, and every message the caller sends is one item of `inbound`, so a Loop over it runs once per message. The opening request comes out on the fixed ports. Declare the item type to have each message checked (`-> (inbound: Generator[Move])`): a message that does not fit is refused back to the caller naming the field, and the session goes on. Answer with Reply per message and Close at the end.

inputs.name: path
inputs.label: Path
inputs.description: Path under the project's live URL: literal segments and `{name}` captures (`chat/{room}`), or empty for the root address. No leading '/'.

inputs.name: dataType
inputs.label: Message shape
inputs.description: What each message is, both ways: `json` (`inbound: Generator[JsonDict]`, a record type, `Generator[Json]` for any JSON value (a list, a bare string or number), or `Generator[Image]` to store a `data:` URL or base64 message), `text` (`Generator[String]`), `bytes` (each binary frame stored, `Generator[File]`).

inputs.name: auth
inputs.label: Check callers with
inputs.description: How a caller is checked on the opening request, before the conversation starts. `none` (the default): anyone with the URL may connect. `api_keys`: one of the connection's keys in `X-Api-Key` or `Authorization: Bearer`; `caller` says which matched (`{"key": 0}` for the first). `hmac_sha256`: `X-Signature` holds the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `<X-Timestamp>.<raw body>` under the connection's secret, a timestamp more than five minutes off refused; `caller` is `{}`. `hmac_sha1` and `hmac_sha512`: the same with that hash. `ed25519`: the same layout, signed with the Ed25519 key whose public half the connection holds; `ecdsa_p256`: signed with ECDSA P-256, the signature in base64 DER. `oidc`: a bearer identity token from the connection's issuer, for its audience; `caller` is the token's claims. A provider's own layout is written as the scheme itself (`{"kind": "api_keys", "header": "X-Team-Key"}`). The secret goes on `connection`.

inputs.name: connection
inputs.label: Connection
inputs.description: What `auth` checks callers against: the accepted keys, the signing secret, the public key, or the issuer and audience. Picked on each install (`weft connect <node>`, or the Connect button), never written in the source. Not used when `auth` is `none`.

inputs.name: maxSessionSecs
inputs.label: Give up on one connection after this long
inputs.description: Hard ceiling on one session, no default: it cuts a live session on the clock. Departures are already caught by the protocol's ping; set it only to cap session length.

inputs.name: callerSilenceSecs
inputs.label: Call the caller gone after this much silence
inputs.description: Seconds the caller's machine may leave sent data unacknowledged before the caller counts as gone. Bounds silence, not session length. Raise for clients whose link sleeps. `0` uses the OS default (about fifteen minutes).

inputs.name: maxInboundMb
inputs.label: Largest message, in MB
inputs.description: Largest single message in MB; a bigger one ends the session with an error.

inputs.name: whenChunkFails
inputs.label: When a message cannot be sent
inputs.description: What happens when a Reply or a Stream cannot turn one message into the socket's `dataType` (a value that is not a String on a `text` socket, a file it cannot read). `surface` (default): that node fails and the socket closes with 1011. `drop_chunk`: that message is skipped, noted on the run's record, and the session goes on; pick it when one missing message is fine, like a frame of a live feed. A run that fails, or a bus that ends failed, closes the socket with 1011 either way.

inputs.name: whenCallerIsSlow
inputs.label: When the caller reads slower than you send
inputs.description: What gives when messages are sent faster than the caller reads them and the 256 messages waiting for it fill up. `block` (default): the next send waits for room, so a slow caller slows the program and gets every message. `drop_oldest`: the oldest waiting message is thrown away, so the caller always gets the latest; pick it for live video or a price feed. `drop_newest`: the new message is thrown away and what was already waiting goes out in order. A dropped message never reaches the caller, so keep `block` for a conversation the caller must read whole.

outputs.name: fired
outputs.description: Always true when a caller connects.

outputs.name: path
outputs.description: Path as called, no leading slash.

outputs.name: headers
outputs.description: Opening request's headers, lowercase names, but the ones carrying a credential, which are on `credentials`.

outputs.name: credentials
outputs.description: The headers carrying a credential (`authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `cookie`, `weft-instance-token`, and those `auth` reads a credential from), lowercase names, each a secret: the run's record holds its marker, never its value. Wire one to a node that takes a secret (an HttpRequest's `headers`), or reveal it in your own node.

outputs.name: caller
outputs.description: Who `auth` found the caller to be: an identity token's claims for `oidc`, `{"key": <index>}` for `api_keys`, `{}` for `hmac` and `signature`. Null when `auth` is `none`.

outputs.name: inbound
outputs.description: One item per caller message, in order; ends when the caller disconnects. Each message is held to the item type declared here (matching `dataType`). A second reader needs a custom node using the ctx (inbound is broadcast there).

then.message: Socket '{id}' takes json messages, each one JSON value (or a picture as a `data:` URL or base64): declare `inbound` as `Generator[<a record type, JsonDict, or Json for any JSON value>]` or `Generator[Image]`, or set `dataType` to the shape the messages have.
Socket '{id}' takes text messages, each one String: declare `-> (inbound: Generator[String])`.
Socket '{id}' takes byte messages, each stored as a file: declare `-> (inbound: Generator[File])`, or the kind they have to be (`Generator[Image]`), which is checked against the bytes.
Socket '{id}' path starts with '/'. The gateway prefixes the route automatically; drop the leading slash.

Socket '{id}' starts a run that never answers its caller: no node that answers it (a Reply, a Stream, a Close) is in it. Wire the answering node so the run reaches it (through data, or `_should_flow` on the node or on the group it sits in).

Socket '{id}' would exist once per instance, because {perInstanceReason}, but its public address is one for every instance. Keep the socket shared and pick the instance per call: the `Weft-Instance` header on a socket gated by a connection, or an instance token.
